newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil seeks to liberalise sugar sector from 98/99.
newsitem.headline: Brazil seeks to liberalise sugar sector from 98/99.

text.p: Brazil's Industry and Commerce Ministry is in favor of liberalising the country's sugar exports but only from the next crop year in 1998/99, said a top government official.

"Our objective is to work to liberalise the sector but we have to work to develop mechanisms for the next crop year (1998/99)," said Mauricio Assis, head of the primary commodities department of the Industry and Commerce Industry.
The government is set to publish its crop plan for the 1997/98 (May/April) sugar harvest on April 30 after a final meeting in Brasilia with private sector representatives this morning, Assis said.
Assis declined to give any figures ahead of the crop plan but said sugar available for export should be a little higher than in 1996/97.
The 1996/97 crop plan allowed for some 5.2 million tonnes of sugar to be sold abroad.
The government is expecting to see a larger crop in terms of sugarcane but wants to direct this increased production into alcohol, thereby eliminating the need for imports.
The government will also this year allow factories to switch between sugar and alcohol exports, depending on which was the more lucrative, Assis said.
"We will allow factories to export the equivalent amount in alcohol as they would have in sugar, should international alcohol prices be more attractive," Assis said.
